title: Refract acceptance contract
description: ai/runs/<run_id>/acceptance.json — the finite list of criteria that decide 'done', written BEFORE any production code (from the spec, the request or the bug report) and then locked by .claude/scripts/lock-acceptance.sh, which hashes this file and every test it names into .claude/locks/<run_id>.json. It holds the contract only: results never live here (a pass flag written after the lock would change the hash the lock protects). Results live in verdict.json, which only the verifier's SubagentStop hook writes. Keywords are the subset .claude/scripts/refract_records.py validates: type, enum, const, required, properties, additionalProperties, items, pattern, minLength, minItems, minimum, maximum, $defs, $ref.

source.description: Where the criteria came from. The verifier reads this file, never the builder's account of it.

ref.description: A spec path or Spec-ID, the plan file, the tracker id, or the request quoted verbatim.

tier.description: T1..T3 for a delivery run (governance/tiers.json; mirrors run.json); trivial / standard / heavy for the pack-lane flows that predate the run.

req.description: The requirement or story id this criterion traces to (REQ-###, a spec story id), when one exists.

ears.description: The criterion as one EARS sentence: WHEN <trigger> THE <system> SHALL <response> (or WHILE / IF … THEN / WHERE). The verifier grades whether the test's assertion expresses THIS sentence, not a proxy for it.

kind.description: regression = a bug-fix criterion: its test must have been seen RED before the fix, in a record test-lane.sh wrote (.claude/evidence/test-runs.jsonl).

tests.description: The test files and cases that prove the criterion. Every `path` is locked with acceptance.json.

command.description: The exact command that runs this criterion's tests at HEAD.

negative.description: true when the criterion asserts a denial or a failure path (a 403, a rejected input).

holdout.description: Reserved for heavy-tier holdout tests kept out of the implementer's view (a later phase); false or absent today.

changes_baseline.description: Stored behaviour this criterion deliberately changes (proposal §7 rule 2): fnmatch patterns over baseline entry ids (`<id>` or `<id>/<case>`, from .claude/baselines/main/manifest.json) or over repo paths of a snapshot / golden file. behavior-diff.py (G14) explains a difference only by a criterion that names it here; test-integrity.py fails a snapshot rewrite no criterion names.

unchanged.description: Existing behaviour this change must NOT alter, one sentence each. The verifier treats a change to any of them as a FAIL unless a criterion declares it.

run_id.description: <YYYYMMDD>-<slug>-<4 hex>, or plan-<plan id> for a /verify-plan run.
